channel.title: Crypto Front Page
channel.description: Crypto Front Page reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto industry.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates after crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake will back 32 House incumbents, including six with $1 million in outside spending, as stalled Senate crypto rules push the industry toward November races.

item.title: Sui backs DATA Network’s move off its own blockchain
item.description: Sui Foundation will invest $30 million as DATA moves its Trace registry and protocol onto Sui, retiring its own chain after a planned phased transition.

item.title: IMF Finds Demand for Tokenized Stocks, Flags Liquidity Risks
item.description: The IMF found tokenized U.S. stocks draw after-hours and fractional trades, while thin liquidity and higher volatility leave market plumbing lagging demand.

item.title: XRP Ledger patched flaw that could create spendable XRP
item.description: XRPL developers fixed an order-book payment flaw that could mint spendable XRP; the patch shipped in September, and no public-network exploitation was found.

item.title: Samsung sets October launch for USDC transfers in Wallet
item.description: Samsung plans to add USDC transfers to Wallet in late October, letting eligible U.S. Galaxy users send to crypto wallets or bank accounts in 60-plus countries.

item.title: ESMA tests tokenised collateral for EU clearing houses
item.description: ESMA opened a call for evidence on tokenised collateral at EU clearing houses, asking how it would work in defaults and what safeguards may be needed.

item.title: FCA opens crypto authorisation window ahead of 2027 rules
item.description: The FCA opened crypto authorisation applications on 30 September, giving firms five months to seek permission before a new UK regime starts in October 2027.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates as crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake will back 32 House members who supported the crypto market-structure bill, naming six for $1 million apiece as the measure stalls in the Senate.

item.title: Fairshake targets 32 House races with crypto spending
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House candidates for midterm support, including six set to receive $1 million each, as Senate efforts to pass crypto market rules stall.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House incumbents after crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake will back 32 House incumbents, including six with $1 million each, as the crypto industry seeks lawmakers to revive stalled market-structure legislation.

item.title: Arbswap and Impermanent Loss: How Pair Prices Diverge
item.description: Impermanent loss compares an AMM position with simply holding its tokens as their relative price moves, while fees and rewards affect the final result.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates after crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House candidates for midterm support, with six slated for $1 million each, as the stalled CLARITY Act leaves crypto rules unresolved.

item.title: Aibai and the mechanics of a first crypto transfer between chains
item.description: Aibai starts with a source chain, destination chain and token; a bridge then locks or burns funds, waits for confirmation and releases or mints the destination asset.

item.title: SEC Approves Cboe Listing of 3x Bitcoin and Ether Funds
item.description: The SEC approved Cboe’s listing rule for Volatility Shares’ 3x Bitcoin and ether funds; they can trade only after registration statements take effect.

item.title: Fairshake commits millions to 32 House candidates
item.description: Fairshake will spend in 32 House races, backing lawmakers who supported crypto market rules as the stalled CLARITY Act leaves the industry seeking a next step.

item.title: What a Bridge Withdrawal Claim Does, Step by Step
item.description: A bridge withdrawal claim proves a Polygon burn was checkpointed and asks Ethereum to release the matching asset; the burn alone does not complete withdrawal.

item.title: Blast to wind down Ethereum layer 2 as costs exceed revenue
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum Layer 2 after saying upkeep costs exceed revenue, with withdrawals paused during a Lido exit and the normal interface available until Oct. 26.

item.title: When to Revoke a Token Spending Approval
item.description: A token approval lets a contract move specified tokens later; revoke it when the job is done, the spender is unfamiliar, or its allowance exceeds what you need.

item.title: SEC proposes new crypto custody routes for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed new custody paths for advisers and funds, including conditional self-custody and state trust companies, with safeguards and a 60-day comment period.

item.title: BNY and Payward discuss broad financial infrastructure pact
item.description: BNY and Kraken parent Payward are discussing a broad services pact spanning custody, trading and payments, but the talks remain private and no deal is assured.
